Claim 1 (Currently amended): A method for treating an ocular condition, the method comprising: administering to the interior of an eye a composition comprising a therapeutically effective amount of a macromolecular anti-angiogenic component (MAAC) to a mammal suffering from an ocular condition, wherein the composition also comprises a viscosity inducing component in an amount effective to increase the viscosity of the composition to a viscosity at about 25°C of at least 10 cps at a shear rate of about 0.1/second, wherein said viscosity inducing component is injectable into the vitreous of a mammalian eye without permanently diminishing visual acuity.

Claim 5 (Currently amended): The method of claim 1 wherein a symptom associated with the ocular condition is angiogenesis and the MAAC comprises a direct or indirect inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) activity.

Claim 6 (Cancelled): The method of claim 5 wherein the MAAC comprises an agent selected from the group consisting of a nucleic acid (an oligonucleotide) and a polypeptide.

Claim 14 (Cancelled): The method of claim 6 wherein said MAAC comprises a protein.

Claim 15 (Cancelled): The method of claim 14 wherein said protein is selected from the group consisting of an antibody, an antibody mimic, an angiogenesis inhibitor and a receptor inhibitor.

Claim 16 (Cancelled): The method of claim 14 wherein said protein comprises a therapeutic agent selected from the group consisting of ADNECTIN® CT-322, ADNECTIN® C7S100, ADNECTIN® C7C100, ranibizumab, bevacizumab, urokinase peptide inhibitor A6, cisplatin, rapamycin, endostatin, angiostatin, tumstatin, pigment epithelium derived factor, and VEGF TRAP® , IMC-18F1 and IMC-1121 Fab.
